Plato was born around **428/427 BC**, at a time of war and political conflict in Athens. He came to know **Socrates**, whose trial and death remained important to his writings, travelled beyond Athens according to accounts of varying reliability, and established the philosophical circle known as the **Academy**.

This guide follows the major episodes of his life without treating every story preserved by ancient biographers as established fact. Understanding Plato's historical setting helps us read the dialogues more carefully—but his life does not provide a simple explanation for every argument they contain.
